rewritten_candidate.content: The long-term memory system is designed with a three-tiered hierarchical structure: L1, L2, and L3. L1 nodes are granular, structured objects from individual meetings. A set of L1s (e.g., from four meetings) are summarized into an L2 node. All L2 nodes are cumulatively summarized into a single, top-level L3 skeleton of the project memory.
rewritten_candidate.rationale: This describes the fundamental architectural decision for the long-term memory system, defining its structure and how information is organized at different levels of granularity. This is a core adopted change in architecture.
